title: draft-ietf-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol-01: HTTP Message Signatures for automated traffic
publisher: IETF Web Bot Auth working group
notes: Datatracker API, read 2026-11-14: rev 01, time 2026-10-29T10:32:27Z, expires 2027-05-02; rev 00 was posted 2026-09-01T13:13:08Z (expiry then 2027-03-05) and was read on 2026-10-11. Authors T. Meunier (Cloudflare), S. Major (Google). Texts read from https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol-01.txt and -00.txt. The -01 changelog makes every Signature-Agent value a direct JWK Set URI and removes the directory, jwks_uri and cimd types; signers must send the Dictionary form (the bare String form is legacy that verifiers may accept); a verifier fetches the member URL directly as a JWK Set (HTTP 200 only, no redirects); the media type application/http-message-signatures-directory+json is required only for a directory at the well-known URI. Unchanged from -00: tag web-bot-auth, covered @authority or @target-uri plus the Signature-Agent member, keyid as a JWK SHA-256 thumbprint, expires recommended within 24 hours, no extra nonce rule, and the test vector with keyid poqkLGiymh_W0uP6PZFw-dvez3QJT5SolqXBCW38r0U.

title: Visa Intelligent Commerce developer documentation (overview, concepts, workflows and production readiness pages)
notes: Replaced the public VIC overview in October 2026. On 2026-10-19 the rendered overview asked visitors to sign in, and its text and the concepts (/docs/visa-intelligent-commerce/concepts) and workflows (/docs/visa-intelligent-commerce/workflows) pages were read from the page source. On 2026-11-14 the overview, concepts, workflows and production-readiness pages and their .md twins answered HTTP 200 with no sign-in prompt. The overview then said production access requires onboarding to VIC and to the Trusted Agent Protocol, Visa Token Service and Visa Payment Passkeys, plus registration through the Visa Agent Registry Service (VARS) so that Visa can validate agent signatures and merchant encryption keys at credential retrieval. The concepts page said agentSignature is required when the agent is a Trusted Agent Provider or the token requestor is a Wallet Provider and is not sent for an Open Source Agent; instructions default to a 30-day intent expiration in the US; at most 15 cryptograms per token in a rolling 24 hours; the restricted MCC list sits in a VIC and TAP Client Implementation Guide, named without a link; and US merchants that support 3-D Secure receive a Program Not Supported response for agentic transactions in the US only, while other regions keep 3DS with region-specific treatment and SCA in Europe uses Visa Payment Passkeys. The production-readiness page said Visa's CE3.0 program covers agentic transactions. Card enrollment journey (read 2026-10-19): token provisioned through VTS first, then issuer step-up where required and, if applicable, Visa Payment Passkey setup with device binding; credential retrieval only after that unless the use case is approved to skip the passkey. Workflows (read 2026-10-19; the authentication step reads the same on 2026-11-14): the consumer authenticates the instruction through a Visa Payment Passkey or other issuer-approved methods; the agent submits the credential to the merchant checkout or a PSP-enabled flow; Visa retains post-purchase confirmation data for disputes. No fees or pricing were stated on either date.

title: Visa Merchant Registry Service (VMRS) in the Trusted Agent Protocol API reference
notes: Read 2026-11-14 (HTTP 200) from this .md twin and from the OpenAPI 3.1.0 document embedded in https://developer.visa.com/api-reference/trusted-agent-protocol/get-v1-trustedagentprotocol (info.title Trusted Agent Protocol, version 1, server https://sandbox.api.visa.com). Tag Visa Merchant Registry Service, described as a micro service that manages merchant identities and distributes encryption keys for payment request encryption in the TAP ecosystem; navigation bundle TRAP.102, public. Nine operations: POST /vmrs/v1/merchants (201; 409 when the merchantUrl already exists; 422); GET and PUT /vmrs/v1/merchants/{merchantId}; GET and POST /vmrs/v1/merchants/{merchantId}/keys (new keys are created deactivated); GET, PUT and DELETE /vmrs/v1/merchants/{merchantId}/keys/{keyId}; POST /vmrs/v1/merchants/{merchantId}/keys/{keyId}/activate. 15 schemas. MerchantCreate requires indicator (TAP, ACG or BOTH; described only as the transaction processing type), merchantName and merchantUrl; optional vmid, encryptionKey (KeyCreate), cryptogramType (TAVV or DAVV, default DAVV), apiIntegrations and webIntegrations (url, integrationSpec, metadata), paymentPayloadType (UNENCRYPTED or ENCRYPTED, default UNENCRYPTED), protocolInteractions (protocol ucp, acp or x402, with url, documentationUrl and metadata) and acceptanceRelationships (example visa, mastercard). KeyCreate requires keyName, algorithm (RSA-OAEP, RSA-OAEP-256, RSA-OAEP-384 or RSA-OAEP-512, a key wrapping algorithm), encryptionKey (a Base64-encoded asymmetric public key in DER, PEM, JWK or OpenSSH format) and encryptionType (A256GCM, A128GCM, C20P, A256CBC_HS512, A128CBC_HS256, A256CCM or A128CCM, a content encryption algorithm); expirationDate is optional and must be in the future. A CredentialsResponse schema (vmid, merchantId, merchantName, merchantUrl, encryptionKey, cryptogramType, paymentPayloadType) is referenced by no path. No security scheme is declared. Not in the reference on 2026-10-19 (see src-visa-tap-apiref).

title: Visa, BILL and Billtrust Launch First Live Pilot for Trusted AI Agent Payments Between Buyer and Supplier Platforms
notes: Business Wire release, Las Vegas, 2026-10-20; read on Visa's newsroom 2026-11-14 (HTTP 200). BILL's and Billtrust's own copies answered 403. The authorized BILL Payment Agent is registered using Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol and Agentic Directory and pays approved supplier invoices with tokenized credentials and controls tied to the buyer's approved payment instructions. Billtrust uses TAP to recognize, authenticate and admit the agent, which Visa says can stand in for CAPTCHA and other bot blocking without an extra agent login. Visa calls it the first live pilot in which trusted AI agents start and complete approved buyer invoice payments end to end through supplier portals (it does not call this the Agentic Directory's first use), and says it is live with participating BILL buyers and Billtrust suppliers. FAQ: no shared supplier-portal logins; the agent only executes eligible payments the buyer already approved. No transaction counts or volumes are given.

title: mppx CHANGELOG.md (entries 0.15.0 to 0.19.0)
notes: Read with git show at origin/main 9405660 (2026-11-14, package version 0.19.0) in research/vendor/mppx. 0.16.0 (793aa2b): request attestation replaced with per-route identity; mppx/attestation became mppx/identity; Mppx.create({ attestation }) removed, and passing it throws; routes take identity: [verifier, ...], for example mppx.charge({ amount, identity: [tap] }); Identity.anyOf added; TAP and Web Bot Auth moved to mppx/extensions/identity/tap and mppx/extensions/identity/web-bot-auth; Client.signer became Client.prover. 0.17.0: payment-stage identity simplified. 0.18.0 (de802b9, 454b9e0): fixed statuses valid, missing (401), invalid (401), forbidden (403) and unavailable (503), with missing now 401 instead of 403; an untrusted or unresolvable signature key is forbidden (403). 0.18.0 (802a27a): tempo.charge(), tempo.session(), tempo.subscription() and tempo() throw at construction when no store is passed and NODE_ENV is production on a multi-instance platform or Cloudflare Workers. 0.19.0 (f2c69d5): the Web Bot Auth and TAP client provers take a key pair (CryptoKeyPair) or a remote Signer instead of a private key alone; Tap.Client.prover keeps keyId. The CHANGELOG gives no dates; npm publish times are in src-visa-tap-npm-mppx.

title: MPP identity documentation (extensions/identity, source of mpp.dev/extensions/identity)
notes: Read with git show at origin/main d062df6 (2026-11-14) in research/vendor/mpp; the file last changed in 91a3996 (2026-11-12). Live at https://mpp.dev/extensions/identity (HTTP 200, 2026-11-14), where https://mpp.dev/advanced/identity now redirects. mppx runs each route verifier at most once per request, before it issues a Challenge, so rejected callers never see payment terms; routes without identity skip identity checks, not payment checks. For agent signatures, an unsigned request or a signature that does not verify gets 401 and a key the resolver does not trust gets 403. The TAP verifier checks the signature, request authority and path, lifetime, intent tag and nonce. The page's TAP client example still passes a private CryptoKey with keyId, the form used before mppx 0.19.0. The earlier sentence that an attestation does not authorize a payment or prove the end user's identity (src-visa-tap-mpp-identity-doc) is not on this page.
